links.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of original discharge summaries versus LLM patient-friendly versions
links.effect: Mean FK grade level 11.0 (SD 1.5) for original summaries vs 6.2 (SD 0.5) for LLM patient-friendly versions (P < .001); PEMAT understandability 13% vs 81%.
links.quote: Mean (SD) Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level was significantly lower in the patient-friendly discharge summaries (6.2 [0.5] vs 11.0 [1.5]; P < .001).

links.outcome: Accuracy, completeness, and safety concerns in LLM-generated patient-friendly discharge summaries
links.effect: 54% of 100 reviews gave the best accuracy rating of 6; 56% rated entirely complete; 18 reviews noted safety concerns, mostly omissions plus some hallucinations.
links.quote: Eighteen reviews noted safety concerns, mostly involving omissions, but also several inaccurate statements (termed hallucinations).

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation of GPT-4 transforming real inpatient discharge summaries to patient-friendly formats, evaluated for readability, understandability, accuracy, and safety by physicians, but without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice comparative arm.
